_comment: The MACHINE-CHECKABLE half of the failures ledger.
Built 2026-08-29 on a measured finding: across this project's sessions, WRITTEN rules
did not prevent repeats (the stale-cwd class was recorded 2026-08-25 and recurred; the
never-pipe rule was in memory AND freshly self-authored and was still broken twice
within the hour), while the PreToolUse hooks blocked every in-scope violation and each
block produced an immediate correction. Advice loses to enforcement, so every class
that can be recognised from the pending command lives here rather than in prose alone.
Each rule is checked against the Bash command ABOUT TO RUN. Only classes that are
recognisable from the command text belong here; judgment classes (reading absence as
fact, reconstructing an identifier, claiming a result from the wrong run) stay prose —
forcing those into regexes produces false positives, and a noisy hook gets deleted.
/harvest-failures appends rules here; no code edit is needed to add one.
kinds: regex | needs_abs_cd | git_foreign_staged | inplace_source_edit | git_source_excerpt

rules.name: stale working directory
rules.message: this runs `make`/`pytest`/`uv run` without establishing its own working directory. The shell's cwd PERSISTS between Bash calls, so a `cd` from an earlier command silently decides where this one runs — it has already produced 'No rule to make target' three times in this project (2026-08-25 twice, 2026-08-28). USE ONE OF THESE, and NOT a leading `cd`: `make -C /Users/sairambkrishnan/git/ondoway <target>`, or an absolute path to the program itself (`/Users/sairambkrishnan/git/ondoway/.venv/bin/python -m pytest /Users/sairambkrishnan/git/ondoway/tests/test_x.py`), or `git -C /Users/sairambkrishnan/git/ondoway ...`. A LEADING `cd /abs &&` CANNOT SATISFY THIS GUARD: measured 2026-08-29, the harness strips a leading `cd` before the command reaches the hook, so eight consecutive attempts to prefix one arrived here as the bare command and were blocked again. Do not retry the `cd` form — it will never pass.

rules.name: Make variable holding multiple paths
rules.message: FILE= holds more than one path. The recipe passes $(FILE) through as ONE quoted argument, so pytest receives a single bogus path and collects zero tests. Use one path per FILE=, chaining separate `make test-file FILE=...` invocations with &&.

rules.name: a saved run log read through a filter
rules.message: a backgrounded run's saved .output log is being piped through a filter. The auditable-tests guard cannot see this (the command names a file, not a test target) and that gap was used 8 times in one session — one keyword filter omitted 'FAILED' and hid two real test failures for a stretch of that session. Read the whole file with the Read tool instead.

rules.name: source content reached through git instead of read
rules.message: this quotes a tracked file's CONTENT through git, which walks around the global whole-source-file guard. Measured 2026-08-29: `grep -n RENDER_LOCAL_EXEC Makefile` was blocked by ~/.claude/hooks/no-grep.py in this session, and `git grep -n RENDER_LOCAL_EXEC Makefile | head -5` ran unchallenged minutes later — that guard looks at the program named `grep`, and `git` is a different program. An excerpt hides the context that changes the correct edit, whichever program prints it. Read the whole file with the Read tool. `git grep -l` (which files match) is allowed and is the way to find the file to read; so are `git log`, `git status`, `git diff`, and an unpiped `git show <rev>:<path>`.

rules.name: project code run with the system interpreter
rules.message: bare `python3` is importing project code. The system python has none of the project's dependencies, so this fails as `ModuleNotFoundError`, which reads exactly like a broken module rather than a wrong interpreter. Use `uv run python`. (`python3 scripts/preflight.py` is exempt by design — preflight is stdlib-only so it can report a missing uv.)

rules.name: a commit that would unstage another session's work
rules.message: the index holds staged entries this command does not name. `git commit -- <paths>` is content-safe but RESETS the index, so a parallel session's staged work is silently unstaged (its file contents survive in the worktree). Measured 2026-08-29 against the owner's own audio-hardening session. Either name them in the pathspec, or proceed deliberately and SAY SO in your report by appending the acknowledgement token to the command.

rules.name: a stream editor rewriting a tracked source file
rules.message: this rewrites a TRACKED source file in place with sed/awk/perl. A stream editor reports SUCCESS when its expression matched nothing, so a wrong expression is silent. Measured 2026-08-29: `sed -i '' 's/...\b.../'` on tests/test_audio_stop_trip_api.py changed nothing because macOS sed has no \b — eleven tests stayed broken, the failure surfaced only on the next full run, and the suite had to be repeated. Use the Edit tool, which fails loudly when its target text is absent, or write the file with a Python script that asserts what it changed. Reading with sed/awk/perl is fine; only in-place writes to tracked files are blocked.
